register: Written-formal and analytical, chiefly with abstract limits, divisions or categories; dépasser is more neutral and broadly usable.
trap: Transcender is directly transitive here (transcender les clivages); se transcender specifically means surpassing oneself and cannot replace it.
example_tl: La coalition affirme transcender les clivages partisans, mais son programme reconduit les mêmes hiérarchies économiques qui structurent depuis longtemps le débat public.
example_en: The coalition claims to transcend partisan divisions, but its program reproduces the same economic hierarchies that have long structured public debate.
cloze: La coalition affirme {{c1::transcender}} les clivages partisans, mais son programme reconduit les mêmes hiérarchies économiques qui structurent depuis longtemps le débat public.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate; the note fixes the formal abstract sense and contrasts it with the more neutral dépasser.

register: Neutral-formal for sustained intellectual or experiential engagement; se plonger dans is slightly less formal and equally idiomatic here.
trap: Immerger without se is transitive and normally submerges something; a person engaging deeply with material s’immerge dans it.
example_tl: Avant de couvrir le procès, la journaliste s’est immergée dans les archives judiciaires afin de comprendre les réseaux d’influence entourant l’ancien ministre.
example_en: Before covering the trial, the journalist immersed herself in the court archives to understand the influence networks surrounding the former minister.
cloze: Avant de couvrir le procès, la journaliste {{c1::s’est immergée dans}} les archives judiciaires afin de comprendre les réseaux d’influence entourant l’ancien ministre.
note: Materially improves old_back, which gives only the transitive verb and omits the pronominal marker and governed preposition required by this sense.

tl: juxtaposer quelque chose à quelque chose
alts: mettre quelque chose en regard de quelque chose
register: Formal analytical vocabulary for placing two claims, texts or facts side by side so that their relationship becomes salient.
trap: The comparison is commonly built as juxtaposer A à B; Spanish yuxtaponer must not produce the nonexistent French form *juxtaponer.
example_tl: L’enquête juxtapose les promesses écologiques du groupe à ses investissements fossiles, révélant un écart persistant entre communication institutionnelle et affectation effective du capital.
example_en: The investigation juxtaposes the group’s environmental promises with its fossil-fuel investments, revealing a persistent gap between institutional messaging and the actual allocation of capital.
cloze: L’enquête {{c1::juxtapose}} les promesses écologiques du groupe {{c1::à}} ses investissements fossiles, révélant un écart persistant entre communication institutionnelle et affectation effective du capital.
note: The legacy verb is valid but incomplete as a production headword; this note supplies its common two-object frame. Self-review: replaced allocation réelle with the more idiomatic affectation effective.

register: Neutral-formal and figurative; éclipser foregrounds one issue drawing attention away from another, while occulter more strongly suggests concealment.
trap: Ombrager concerns literal shade or shelter from the sun; it does not express the figurative attention-displacing sense of English overshadow.
example_tl: La polémique entourant l’application a éclipsé les conséquences sociales de sa fermeture, notamment la disparition de services essentiels dans plusieurs quartiers populaires.
example_en: The controversy surrounding the app overshadowed the social consequences of its closure, notably the disappearance of essential services in several working-class neighborhoods.
cloze: La polémique entourant l’application a {{c1::éclipsé}} les conséquences sociales de sa fermeture, notamment la disparition de services essentiels dans plusieurs quartiers populaires.
note: Old_back selects the intended figurative sense correctly; the example makes the attention hierarchy explicit.

register: Neutral-formal in organizational criticism; cloisonner is especially idiomatic for teams, information or responsibilities kept in separate silos.
trap: English-based *compartimentaliser is not standard French; compartimenter exists, while cloisonner is often more idiomatic for organizational separation.
example_tl: L’administration a cloisonné les équipes chargées de l’algorithme, empêchant les juristes d’évaluer les choix techniques avant le déploiement du système.
example_en: The administration compartmentalized the teams responsible for the algorithm, preventing lawyers from assessing the technical choices before the system was deployed.
cloze: L’administration a {{c1::cloisonné}} les équipes chargées de l’algorithme, empêchant les juristes d’évaluer les choix techniques avant le déploiement du système.
note: Materially diverges from old_back by preferring cloisonner for the organizational sense; compartimenter remains a valid, slightly more technical alternative.

tl: replacer quelque chose dans son contexte
register: Neutral-formal analytical prose; the explicit frame is less jargony than contextualiser and is natural in historical or policy writing.
example_tl: L’historienne replace la réforme dans son contexte, rappelant que les coupes imposées aux médias publics précédaient largement l’essor des plateformes numériques.
example_en: The historian places the reform in context, recalling that the cuts imposed on public media long predated the rise of digital platforms.
cloze: L’historienne {{c1::replace}} la réforme {{c1::dans son contexte}}, rappelant que les coupes imposées aux médias publics précédaient largement l’essor des plateformes numériques.
note: Old_back is valid, but the production headword adds a less jargony idiomatic frame. Self-review: removed an adjective after contexte so contextualiser remains a clean alternative in the example.

register: Neutral-formal for a result, position or practice departing from a reference point; diverger de is especially analytical.
trap: S’écarter requires de; unlike Spanish desviarse, standard French dévier is non-pronominal, so use dévier or s’écarter rather than *se dévier.
example_tl: Les résultats observés s’écartent nettement des projections officielles, ce qui fragilise l’argument selon lequel la réforme devait réduire les inégalités territoriales.
example_en: The observed results deviate markedly from the official projections, weakening the argument that the reform was supposed to reduce territorial inequalities.
cloze: Les résultats observés {{c1::s’écartent}} nettement {{c1::des}} projections officielles, ce qui fragilise l’argument selon lequel la réforme devait réduire les inégalités territoriales.
note: The isolated source is polysemous. This note selects abstract departure from a reference point; old_back remains valid for a path or trajectory changing direction.

register: Neutral-formal and idiomatic for an argument or message eliciting recognition from a particular audience.
trap: French résonner is intransitive and cannot take the audience as a direct object; the audience is introduced by auprès de or chez in this sense.
example_tl: Le plaidoyer des chercheurs a trouvé un écho auprès des élus locaux, confrontés quotidiennement aux effets de la désinformation sur les services publics.
example_en: The researchers’ plea resonated with local elected officials, who face the effects of disinformation on public services every day.
cloze: Le plaidoyer des chercheurs {{c1::a trouvé un écho auprès des}} élus locaux, confrontés quotidiennement aux effets de la désinformation sur les services publics.
note: Materially diverges from the literal legacy verb by selecting the idiomatic audience-response sense rather than literal acoustic resonance.

register: Formal in political theory, geopolitics and market analysis; domination is broader and less theoretically marked.
trap: A controlled domain is expressed in the frame l’hégémonie de X sur Y; as a French common noun, hégémonie remains lowercase.
example_tl: Plusieurs États cherchent à contester l’hégémonie des grandes plateformes sur l’infrastructure informationnelle, sans disposer encore d’alternatives techniques ni financières crédibles.
example_en: Several states are seeking to challenge the hegemony of major platforms over information infrastructure, without yet having credible technical or financial alternatives.
cloze: Plusieurs États cherchent à contester {{c1::l’hégémonie}} des grandes plateformes sur l’infrastructure informationnelle, sans disposer encore d’alternatives techniques ni financières crédibles.
note: The legacy lexeme is accurate; the note normalizes its capitalization and fixes the common de X sur Y complement pattern.

register: Formal legal and geopolitical vocabulary for supreme authority over a territory or domain; also productive in debates on digital and data policy.
trap: Souveraineté is not a blanket synonym for autonomie or indépendance: it foregrounds ultimate rule-making authority, commonly expressed as souveraineté sur a domain.
example_tl: Le règlement affirme la souveraineté européenne sur les données stratégiques, tout en laissant aux fournisseurs étrangers le contrôle matériel des infrastructures essentielles.
example_en: The regulation asserts European sovereignty over strategic data while leaving foreign providers with material control of essential infrastructure.
cloze: Le règlement affirme {{c1::la souveraineté}} européenne sur les données stratégiques, tout en laissant aux fournisseurs étrangers le contrôle matériel des infrastructures essentielles.
note: The legacy rendering is lexically correct; the note normalizes capitalization and distinguishes sovereign authority from mere operational autonomy.

register: Formal and technical for compliance with a standard or requirement; social conformity is normally conformisme or, more neutrally, adaptation au groupe.
trap: English conformity can denote either technical conformité à a rule or social conformisme; French keeps those senses lexically distinct.
example_tl: L’audit vérifie la conformité du système aux normes européennes, mais n’évalue ni les biais du modèle ni les conditions de travail des annotateurs.
example_en: The audit verifies the system’s conformity with European standards but assesses neither the model’s biases nor the annotators’ working conditions.
cloze: L’audit vérifie {{c1::la conformité}} du système {{c1::aux}} normes européennes, mais n’évalue ni les biais du modèle ni les conditions de travail des annotateurs.
note: The source is polysemous. This note selects regulatory conformity and adds the governed à complement omitted by old_back.

register: Neutral in journalism, law and digital policy; it denotes the condition of an unidentified or unnamed person or source.
trap: French normally uses masculine anonymat; anonymité is obsolete and should not be revived as an English-influenced production form.
example_tl: L’anonymat des sources protège les lanceurs d’alerte, mais il impose aux rédactions des procédures rigoureuses pour vérifier les documents et prévenir les manipulations.
example_en: Source anonymity protects whistleblowers, but it requires newsrooms to follow rigorous procedures for verifying documents and preventing manipulation.
cloze: {{c1::L’anonymat}} des sources protège les lanceurs d’alerte, mais il impose aux rédactions des procédures rigoureuses pour vérifier les documents et prévenir les manipulations.
note: Old_back is accurate. Retention is justified by the noncognate French formation and masculine gender, both absent from the English prompt.

register: Neutral-formal in legal, political and media analysis; équivoque can imply a more suspiciously double or unclear reading.
trap: Write ambiguïté with a diaeresis; Spanish ambigüedad must not prompt *ambigüité, and the feminine adjective is ambiguë.
example_tl: L’ambiguïté de la directive permet aux plateformes d’invoquer tantôt la sécurité des usagers, tantôt la liberté d’expression, selon leurs intérêts commerciaux.
example_en: The directive’s ambiguity allows platforms to invoke user safety at times and freedom of expression at others, depending on their commercial interests.
cloze: {{c1::L’ambiguïté}} de la directive permet aux plateformes d’invoquer tantôt la sécurité des usagers, tantôt la liberté d’expression, selon leurs intérêts commerciaux.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate. The production value lies in the French spelling and in distinguishing neutral ambiguity from a deliberately equivocal formulation.

register: Specialist masculine noun in sociology, rhetoric and media criticism for the characteristic dispositions or culture of a group; the accented spelling also occurs.
trap: Ethos is masculine and does not mean éthique: ethos describes a characteristic collective orientation, whereas éthique concerns moral principles or reflection.
example_tl: L’ethos de la rédaction s’est érodé lorsque la direction a subordonné l’indépendance éditoriale aux objectifs trimestriels fixés par les nouveaux actionnaires.
example_en: The newsroom’s ethos eroded when management subordinated editorial independence to the quarterly targets set by the new shareholders.
cloze: {{c1::L’ethos}} de la rédaction s’est érodé lorsque la direction a subordonné l’indépendance éditoriale aux objectifs trimestriels fixés par les nouveaux actionnaires.
note: Modern references vary between ethos and éthos. This note follows the unaccented Larousse monolingual headword, records the accented variant, and corrects old_back’s capitalization.

register: Neutral-formal in political, social and media analysis; morcellement more concretely foregrounds division into separate pieces.
trap: Fragmentation is not polarisation: fragmentation creates multiple separated segments, whereas polarisation organizes positions around opposing poles.
example_tl: La fragmentation de l’espace médiatique multiplie les publics isolés, sans pour autant garantir la diversité éditoriale ni réduire le pouvoir des principaux intermédiaires.
example_en: The fragmentation of the media landscape multiplies isolated audiences without necessarily guaranteeing editorial diversity or reducing the power of the main intermediaries.
cloze: {{c1::La fragmentation}} de l’espace médiatique multiplie les publics isolés, sans pour autant garantir la diversité éditoriale ni réduire le pouvoir des principaux intermédiaires.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate. The noun is retained for its established social-analysis sense; the transparent verb was dropped earlier in this chunk.

register: Marked critical vocabulary in political economy, sociology and media studies for converting something previously outside the market into a commodity.
trap: Commercialisation concerns marketing or selling an existing product; it does not by itself express the conversion of attention or care into a commodity.
example_tl: La marchandisation de l’attention transforme chaque geste en donnée exploitable et pousse les plateformes à privilégier l’engagement compulsif au détriment de la délibération.
example_en: The commodification of attention turns every action into exploitable data and pushes platforms to favor compulsive engagement at the expense of deliberation.
cloze: {{c1::La marchandisation}} de l’attention transforme chaque geste en donnée exploitable et pousse les plateformes à privilégier l’engagement compulsif au détriment de la délibération.
note: The nonliteral legacy rendering is accurate; the note preserves the narrower critical sense rather than weakening it to commercialisation.

register: Neutral-formal; in verification contexts it concerns whether an object or record is genuine, not whether its accompanying claim is true.
trap: Authenticité, véracité and sincérité differ: a video can be authentic, its caption false, and the person sharing it sincere.
example_tl: Les journalistes ont vérifié l’authenticité des vidéos avant publication, sans pouvoir confirmer la véracité des légendes ajoutées par les comptes qui les diffusaient.
example_en: The journalists verified the videos’ authenticity before publication without being able to confirm the truthfulness of the captions added by the accounts distributing them.
cloze: Les journalistes ont vérifié {{c1::l’authenticité}} des vidéos avant publication, sans pouvoir confirmer la véracité des légendes ajoutées par les comptes qui les diffusaient.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate. Self-review: replaced comptes diffuseurs with idiomatic comptes qui les diffusaient and separated authenticity of the media object from truth of the attached claim.

register: Specialist but standard in technical and regulatory prose for systems able to exchange information and make operational use of it.
trap: Compatibilité is weaker: two systems may coexist or accept the same format without exchanging and using data as interoperable systems do.
example_tl: Le règlement impose l’interopérabilité des messageries dominantes afin que les usagers puissent communiquer entre services sans abandonner leurs contacts ni leurs historiques.
example_en: The regulation requires interoperability among dominant messaging services so users can communicate across services without abandoning their contacts or histories.
cloze: Le règlement impose {{c1::l’interopérabilité}} des messageries dominantes afin que les usagers puissent communiquer entre services sans abandonner leurs contacts ni leurs historiques.
note: Old_back is accurate. Retention is justified by the term’s precise regulatory meaning and its consequential distinction from mere compatibility.

register: Written-formal in philosophy and media theory for an apparently direct experience or relationship without an acknowledged intermediary.
trap: In this media-theoretical sense, immédiateté means lack of mediation or distance, not urgency, which is urgence or caractère pressant.
example_tl: L’apparente immédiateté des retransmissions en direct masque les choix de cadrage, de montage et de diffusion algorithmique qui façonnent notre perception des crises.
example_en: The apparent immediacy of live broadcasts conceals the framing, editing, and algorithmic distribution choices that shape our perception of crises.
cloze: L’apparente {{c1::immédiateté}} des retransmissions en direct masque les choix de cadrage, de montage et de diffusion algorithmique qui façonnent notre perception des crises.
note: Old_back is accurate for the media-theoretical sense fixed here. Self-review: replaced des directs with des retransmissions en direct to match the written-formal register.

register: Formal analytical vocabulary; homogénéisation stresses a process of growing similarity, while uniformisation more strongly suggests a uniform outcome.
trap: Homogénéisation does not necessarily imply compliance with a formal standard; that institutional process is more precisely normalisation or standardisation.
example_tl: L’homogénéisation des formats éditoriaux facilite leur circulation internationale, mais elle efface progressivement les conventions narratives et les priorités politiques propres à chaque marché.
example_en: The homogenization of editorial formats facilitates their international circulation, but it gradually erases the narrative conventions and political priorities specific to each market.
cloze: {{c1::L’homogénéisation}} des formats éditoriaux facilite leur circulation internationale, mais elle efface progressivement les conventions narratives et les priorités politiques propres à chaque marché.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate. Self-review: retained uniformisation only as a near-equivalent and stated its stronger emphasis on uniform outcomes.
